thread:
jae: quick proposal — we should cap policy decision CPU time to a tight "decision-time budget" and slot requests into small decision windows. motivation: long policy evals => tail latency and lost SLA. thoughts?

maria: +1 on budgeted decisions. can you sketch how this interacts w/ batching and KV cache hits?

jae: the mental model: every route decision gets X ms (configurable). if a decision exceeds X we fall back to a fast-path policy (less accurate but deterministic) and return earlier. batching still runs upstream for serving, but router returns early with chosen variant. KV/cache unaffected, still used by chosen model.

devon: how do we pick X? per-tenant vs global?

jae: propose defaults: 20ms global base, tenant overrides for enterprise tiers -> up to 50ms. also provide adaptive windowing: if runtime sees lots of p95 policy eval > budget, enlarge window for that tenant gradually.

sam: curious about cost tradeoffs. longer decision time might reduce model token cost (pick cheaper model) but increases endpoint latency. need to quantify.

jae: exactly. we should expose two knobs: decision_time_budget_ms and decision_cost_threshold. runtime will estimate delta-cost of active choices and abort if decision_time > budget AND estimated_cost_savings < threshold.

maria: can you show a mock config?

jae: sure — example config snippet:

```
router: 
  decision_time_budget_ms: 20
  fallback_policy: quick-route
  adaptive_window: true
  slot_size_ms: 5   # micro-slots used to preempt long evals
  decision_cost_threshold_usd_per_100k: 0.50
```

devon: slotting sounds interesting. do you mean we run policy evaluation in increments and release partial results?

jae: yes. implement a cooperative eval model: the compiler/runtime yields at slot boundaries so heavy matchers can be paused and resumed or preempted. if time runs out, we use the best-so-far score.

sam: how to test correctness? edgecase: long-running eval finds a geo-specific cheaper route; quick-path chooses local cheaper path => different behavior. we need replayable sim.

jae: agree. propose a sim harness that replays production traces and runs (1) full-policy without budget, (2) budgeted-policy. measure deltas: route-divergence, cost delta, latency delta, and SLO breaches.

maria: telemetry required: per-decision latency histogram, fallback-rate, best-so-far-score-at-abort, per-tenant adaptive-window adjustments.

ops-bot: created ticket INF-4612: "Decision-time-budget simulation harness + telemetry" — assignee: devon.

devon: I'll own the sim and the replay infra. estimate 2 sprints for initial metrics.

infra-bot: CI:policy-e2e pipeline queued for branch jae/decision-budget (job 4821).

sam: rollout plan idea: feature-flagged rollout, start with read-only shadow mode (compute decision but don't enforce), kibana dashboard, then enable soft-fallback, then hard enforce for low-tier tenants.

maria: one more: need a safety valve — if fallback_rate spikes > 3% cluster-wide for 10m, auto-disable budgeted-path and send page.

jae: good call. add circuit breaker metric + auto-rollback. also add an opt-out per-tenant flag for customers that want deterministic routing.

devon: raises: metric cardinality — we should aggregate by tenant-hash instead of raw tenant id for high-cardinality tenants.

jae: agreed. use hashed_tenant + tier label.

sam: can we add an offline eval that uses a longer decision_time and then computes "regret" (cost difference) for each budget config? that will help set decision_cost_threshold.

jae: yes — that's part of sim plan.

maria: ok cool. next steps: devon + jae to prototype sim and slotting API. sam to draft SLA/cost tradeoff doc for product. I'll add rollout checklist.

devon: pulling it into sprint planning. thanks. :thumbsup:

jae: thanks all. filing RFC follow-up with details and example logs we need.

ops-bot: incident note: none.
